## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# Climb batch 6.5

## 1. For Pavol

Batch 6.5 is the repair batch of the plan's phase 2b: what the conformance reviews of batches 3 to 6 found, with three findings of the reviews of batches 6b, 7 and 7R, repaired before phase 3 (`explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md`, phase 2b). A rung is one fix, built test-first by one worker in its own copy of the tree and judged by a second worker, the skeptic, before the batch is merged and the whole test suite (the gate) runs once.

In plain words: the batch fixes six defects of the compiled path that the switch-over and microGPT's parallel run would meet (a class-loading race at four threads, a parallel task and a generic method that fail to load, two dispatch defects, and a `typecase` whose bound name the code generator never binds, which is why the compiled `cast` never matched); makes both paths refuse a size beyond `NN32` as you decided; makes walk's last integer natives, `LCM` on the unsigned types, `^` and `CHOOSE`, raise `IntegerOverflow` where the result does not fit, instead of a wrong number or an error no `catch` sees; repairs the range bodies that relied on wrapping, with the reorder you chose for the strided distance; makes `RR32` a sibling of `RR64` as the specification and the team's own compiler library have it; and brings the specification and our test messages up to date with what earlier batches built. It runs as two runs of one record, G and P first and then E and V from the tree they land: G first as you decided, and P and V apart because they edit the same two specification files, while a run of all four would be the longest yet; one word runs the four as one (below).

**No question is open.** The draft's one question, when walk switches a numeral to `IntLiteral`, which the probe showed cannot happen before answer 8's promotion rule on either path (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-6.5/NOTES.md`, section 1), you answered on 2026-09-27: batch N builds the inference rule, whose number case is the promotion rule, together with the numeral switch, on both paths, and that closes this question (POSITIONS 2026-09-27, the numerics plans, decision 3; `explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md`, phase 3, item 4). So this batch writes row 443's owed test, rung G makes answer 7's identities independent of a numeral's type, and rows 79, 432, 437 and 443 stay open for batch N.

**The rungs.**
- **G, generics at run time on the compiled path.** The class loader's first-load race at four threads (row 417), a parallel task in a generic declaration (row 419), a generic method building over two sets of parameters (row 420), the two dispatch defects with the measured 43-line fix, and a `typecase` or `catch` clause's bound name (row 351, which is the cause of row 426, at `cast` and at the library's second such clause, `andCondCombine`); answer 7's identity functions made to pass values of the right type through `cast`.
- **P, the text.** The specification gains the integer rules you decided on 2026-09-22 (the shifts, `narrow`, the overflow of an unrepresentable shift) and a corrected coercion example (row 394); the rational type's listing states the algebra the library declares; the test messages whose specification line numbers earlier batches moved are re-anchored; the scalar block's comment stops naming a shape answer 9 refuses; and the owed expected-failure tests of rows 440 and 443 are written.
- **E, a value beyond its type's range.** Both paths refuse a size beyond `NN32` (`ZZ32` for an `int` size), and walk reads the sizes in range exactly, where today it truncates them to 32 bits (row 418); `NN32`'s `LCM` raises `IntegerOverflow` where the result does not fit, instead of a wrong number, and so do the nine natives rung O left, `^` and `CHOOSE` on the four fixed widths and `NN64`'s `LCM` (row 347 closes with them); and the three range bodies that answered right at the integer bounds only by wrapping, with the sequential ranges that step past their last element, are reordered on the checked operators, as you decided for the strided distance (rows 450, 451).
- **V, `RR32` a sibling.** `RR32` stops being a subtype of `RR64`; `RR64` converts from it; its arithmetic takes an `RR32` (row 435); one sentence in the number chapter names it.

**Read from the record, not asked.** Each follows from a decision on record or from a probe; one word from you changes it.
- **Two runs.** The first run, batch 6.5, is G and P; the second, batch 6.5b, is E and V, cut from the tree the first lands. G goes first by your decision: its rows (417, 419, 420, 351, 426) are on microGPT's compiled run (POSITIONS 2026-09-27, the numerics plans, decision 5; `explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md`, phase 2b), and batch N may take the slot after this run. The rule that a batch carries one rung touching Java or Scala (`explorations/coordinator/batched-climb-plan.md` section 5, rule 3) does not force the split: its reason is the cost of a full rebuild in each copy, and batches 3.5, 4 and 5 ran two such rungs, as batch 7's second run, batch 7b, will (C and W). Two things do. P and V both edit `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex`, and both add their Appendix I entries at one place of `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, after its last revision entry, since batch 7C rung X's "The traits that extend a closed trait" (`:1246` at cd9305c2d), before "Passages not yet revised" (`:1340`), which in one run is a same-point hunk the gather resolves by hand (section 4). And a run of the four is 8 to 11 hours in one piece, with G the largest rung, under a container that has died before (`explorations/coordinator/remote-container.md`), with a held push holding four rungs instead of two. So each run pairs the rung in Java or Scala with one that is not, G with P and E with V, and neither pair shares a declaration (section 4). The price of the split is one more gather and gate, about 8 agents, 2M tokens and 2 hours. One word runs the four as one batch (section 7's `RUN`), with section 4's order for the two shared files.
- **Rows 450 and 451 go to E.** Their repair is decided: the distance reordered so that no step leaves the range, the checked operators kept, and emptiness tested before the distance, as you decided for the strided distance (POSITIONS 2026-09-26, rung O of climb batch 4; the rows' notes). Rung O's batch and batch 7R each left them out of their rungs, and at the switch-over the compiled path runs these bodies (`explorations/reviews/batch-6b-7-conformance.md` finding 2, `explorations/reviews/batch-7R-conformance.md` finding 5). E or P could carry them under the batch rules: in either run the bodies share no declaration with the other rung's edits, and they are Fortress, so each run keeps one rung in Java or Scala. E carries them because a change to every sequential range's step needs the interpreter corpus compared before and after, which E runs anyway for its natives, so one comparison measures both; P stays a text rung whose checker count cannot move. In the second run E and V then share `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` on declarations far apart (section 4).
- **E takes the nine natives rung O left.** By reading, `^` and `CHOOSE` on the four fixed widths and `NN64`'s `LCM` still answer a wrong number or raise an error no `catch` sees (rung O's `REPORT.md` section 3; `explorations/reviews/batch-6b-7-conformance.md` finding 3). The specification settles them (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:154-155`), and walk raises its catchable `IntegerOverflow` for them by the rule of your decisions on row 379 and on the unsigned types (POSITIONS 2026-09-24, ledger row 379; 2026-09-26, the fifth batch-5 answer), which rung O built for the arithmetic natives. They share `NN32.java` and one test with `NN32`'s `LCM`, which E already carries. They get one new row, which closes with them, and row 347 closes if `Int$Pow` and `Int$Choose` are its last uncatchable callers, as the review reads.
- **Row 426 fits this batch.** Its cause, traced by the probe, is two things: the code generator never binds a `typecase` clause's name (row 351, whose fix is recorded in the row), and `cast[\ZZ32\](0)` passes a numeral, which is correctly not a `ZZ32` on the compiled path (`NOTES.md`, section 2). Both are small, so G carries them. What waits for the switch-over is only the end-to-end check of a compiled `SUM`'s identity, because the compiler's own library has no generic `SUM`.
- **`RR32` a sibling needs no question.** The specification says the number types are mutually exclusive (`Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:536`), the later Types chapter keeps that (`Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick:977-978`), Chase cut the subtype in 2009 ("RR32 is NOT a subtype of RR64", `6896886fb`), Steele's retrospective draws the two floats as siblings, the compiler library has `RR64` converting from `RR32`, the specification's own worked example converts an `RR32` into `RR64` arithmetic, and your answer 8's rule makes an exact conversion a coercion. The probe found nothing that relies on the subtype beyond `RR32`'s own declarations and three library sites, which the rung restates (`NOTES.md`, section 6); with `RR32`'s operators declared in its api as `RR64`'s are, the corpus changes no verdict but that of row 435's expected failure, which passes, and no team test line.
- **A size read as a value keeps the checker's type.** Your decision's words, a `nat` parameter "is an `NN32` value", admit two readings, the range alone or the type as well. The record takes the range: a size beyond `NN32` is refused, and the compiled checker keeps typing a size read as a value as `IntLiteral`, which converts into `NN32` wherever the specification's sentence names. Typing it `NN32` itself would refuse, at the switch-over, the one library's own bodies that read a size into `ZZ32` index arithmetic (`for i <- seq(1#(s0-1))` at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2426` and `:2807`, `b0#s0` at `:2462` and `:2470`, `self[0#n]` at `:4102`), where an `NN32` beside a `ZZ32` needs batch N's inference rule, and about 16 compiled test files that read a size into `ZZ32` or `ZZ64`, a conversion the compiler library lacks. It comes back with batch N's numeral switch and the array design; `PLAN.md`'s item 25, whether a `nat` parameter may be a range's component, is the same question asked from the range's side, which the review of batch 7R asks to settle before batch N (its finding 1).
- **The rational type's listing states the library's algebra.** The number chapters describe the one library (your answer 6 and the rule that the gather checks the chapters against the library), and the library's `QQ` carries the group, ring and order traits `SUM` and `PROD` need. The chapter's listing gives `QQ` only `Number`, because 0/0 breaks the laws; P states the library's traits with one sentence that their laws hold away from 0/0 and the infinities, as `RR64`'s hold away from NaN. Your parked question on whether `QQ` holds 0/0 at all is untouched.
- **The integer rules go into the specification's prose, in the team's layered form (S1),** as every change to the specification since rung S (POSITIONS 2026-09-24, the requirement on the plan).
- **The stops are reversible.** Each stop this record reserves for you lands and is listed for your review; none holds a push or the next run (POSITIONS 2026-09-27, the stops; the protocol's first hard rule).
- **Row 417's gated home is a program in the gate's four-thread stage,** as phase 2b says. The stage is in the script, outside the manifest, so the coordinator makes that change with the first run's splice, since G runs first (section 8).
- **The dispatch fix covers template dispatchers, as measured.** The probe re-ran it on today's tree: the three legal programs that die today print the specification's answers. Generic dotted methods and a dispatcher that is not a template keep the defect; G records them.

**What the batch leaves out.**
- The numeral switch, batch N's (section 1), and with it rows 79, 432 and 437 and PLAN's item 19.
- From the reviews, what the plan already holds elsewhere: the checked narrowing after the switch-over and the `asString` overflow (phase 4); the product-of-sizes storage (item 15); rung C's two points (item 16); the where-clause sentence (item 14); rows 446 and 447 (items 17 and 18); a judge striking a candidate (asked 2026-09-27).
- The tuple shifts of `Library/RangeInternals.fss` that subtract a whole tuple (batch 3.5 and 4's review, smaller findings): no row and no probe yet.
- Row 453, the compiler prelude's range midpoint and its `#` at the integer bounds: the prelude leaves at the switch-over, and E's repair of the one library's bodies is what the compiled path then runs.
- Record repairs the reviews name (the stale `FACTS.md` line on the exclusion fork, row 97's note, row 360's options): the coordinator's record work, not a rung.
- Row 424's repair, row 433's fusion pairs and row 441: phase 3 or later, as the plan has them.

**Cost.** By arithmetic, not measured, from the batch records: a rung costs 3 to 5 agents, 1.0M to 2.0M tokens and 1.2 to 2.0 hours of the two-agent queue, and a run's tail from the gather to the commit about 8 agents, 2M tokens and 2 hours (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-7.md` section 1, "Cost"). The first run, G and P: 16 to 20 agents, 5M to 8M tokens, 5 to 8 hours, G being the largest rung. The second, E and V: 14 to 18 agents, 5M to 8M tokens, 5 to 8 hours, each rung with three passes over the interpreter corpus (30 to 34 minutes a pass on this box, `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-6.5/probes/rr32/passes-machine.txt`), which load the box together where they overlap. As one run of four: 20 to 28 agents, 7M to 11M tokens, 8 to 11 hours, one tail fewer. The probes cost about 1M tokens. Two agents run at a time; the box has 4 CPUs, 16 GB and 11 GB of free disk at the review (`df -h /`, the probes' worktrees removed, batch 6b's still present).

**What "go" commits you to.** Two gos, one per run. The first: the compiled path's class loader takes a lock on first load, and parallel tasks, generic methods, dispatch and `typecase` bindings work where they failed; answer 7's identity functions are respelled with the same values; the gate's four-thread stage gains G's program; the specification states the integer rules of 2026-09-22 and a corrected example, in the S1 form; the rational type's listing states the library's traits; a handful of our test messages get new line numbers; the scalar block's comment is reworded; two expected-failure tests are added. The second: both paths refuse a size beyond `NN32`, and walk reads the sizes in range exactly; walk's `LCM`, `^` and `CHOOSE` raise instead of wrapping or failing where no `catch` sees it; the range bodies that relied on wrapping are reordered, and their three expected failures pass; `RR32` is a sibling of `RR64`. In both: no model line changes; rows 351, 417, 418, 419, 426, 435, 450 and 451 close, row 420 if G repairs it and row 347 if E's reading holds; the dispatch defects, the `LCM` defect and the nine natives get rows that close in the batch.

## 2. The decisions this batch carries

Cited by date and entry name in `explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md`.
- **The repair batch**, 2026-09-27, in `explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md`, phase 2b: what the reviews of batches 3 to 6 call for is repaired before phase 3, "planned by one Opus worker, reviewed in place by Fable, launched on his go"; its list is this batch's list, with batch 6's review added and three findings of the reviews of 2026-09-28 (section 5).

And the design principle of 2026-09-22: JVM defaults where they make sense, corrected where precision matters.

10	
11	## 1. What is fixed
12	
13	All six, on the compiled path:
14	
15	1. **Row 417, the first-load race.** `InstantiatingClassloader.loadClass` now runs under `getClassLoadingLock(name)`, the lock the JDK's own `ClassLoader.loadClass` takes and this override had dropped. `FirstLoadThreadsRungG` fails 5 of 5 compiled runs at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4` on the base (`threads-before.txt:10-14`, `NullPointerException ... "cl" is null`) and passes 5 of 5 after (`threads-after.txt:10-14`); both pass at one thread. Rung Z's `ZsThreadsT`, `ZsThreadsS`, `ZsThreads` and the control `ZsThreadsLit` pass 5 of 5 at both counts (`threads-zs-after.txt`), and a 24-instantiation widening passes 5 of 5 (`FirstLoad24.fss`, `threads-24-after.txt`).
16	2. **Row 419, a task in a generic declaration.** The measured 13-line patch: `delegate` makes the task class generic over the task's free static parameters, as `forFnExpr` does for a closure. `NatRtTask` (promoted from `XXXNatRtTask`) passes.
17	3. **Row 420, a generic method building over two parameter sets.** Its site is row 419's: the method's `||` operands are run as a task, and the task class was not generic. Disassembled on the base, the method template `H☝m⟦☝,U,T⟧` builds its second operand in the non-generic `ZrMethNoClosureT$task0`, which names `U`. Two controls on the base settle it (`row420-cause-before.txt`): the method's own parameter alone, in two task operands, fails the same way (`MethOneParTask`, `U$RTTIc`), and both parameters with no task operand pass (`MethBothNoTask`, `stringzz32`). 28	## 3. Where each fix belongs (rule 1)

Its explicit callers are `RTHelpers.loadClosureClass` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/RTHelpers.java:133`), `RTHelpers.getRTTIclass` (`:49`) and the union instantiation (`InstantiatingClassloader.java:1921`). The parallelism analyzer's operands reach the same `forExprsParallel`, whose one call of `delegate` (`CodeGen.java:1638`) makes every task class. The three dispatch programs are α-equivalent pairs (`pair[\B,A\]` is `pair[\A,B\]` renamed). They are legal under this text as it stands and under answer 9's positional rule (POSITIONS.md:108, 2026-09-26, answer 9). The specification's answers are the assertions of the three tests.
39	- **Row 419.** Static parameters "are in scope of the entire body of the declaration" (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:19-24`), and each `also` block is "run in a separate implicit thread" (`Specification/basic/expressions/also.tex:17-21`). A task body therefore sees the declaration's static parameters.
40	- **Row 351, catch site.** "The exception value is bound to the identifier specified in the catch clause" (`Specification/basic/expressions/try.tex:56-60`).

The prose is written for the `typecase x = e of` spelling. 150	## 12. Decisions, each with the ways not taken
151	
152	- **The lock's shape.** Candidates:
153	  - `synchronized (getClassLoadingLock(name))` around the whole of `loadClass`, which is the loader's own monitor. Taken.
154	  - The same with `registerAsParallelCapable`, one lock per name.
155	  - A lock only in `loadClosureClass`.
156	  - A `ConcurrentHashMap` of futures per name.
157	
158	  The monitor is the lock the JVM already holds when it resolves a class through a loader that is not parallel-capable, and it is what the JDK's own `loadClass` takes. Explicit loads (`loadClosureClass`, `getRTTIclass`, the union instantiation) were the only ones running without it. Taking it adds no lock order the implicit loads do not already have: a generation step that initialises another class under the monitor, as `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/MethodInstantiater.java:274` can, already does so on every implicit load. Per-name locks would admit two loads each holding one name's lock while generating a class that needs the other's; the JDK leaves them off unless a loader opts in. A lock in `loadClosureClass` alone leaves the other two explicit callers racing. Futures would change the loader's structure for no gain the measurement can see.
159	- **Where `history` is written.** Left before `defineClass`. Under the lock no other thread can see the name before its class is defined. Moving the write would change what the same thread does if generation re-enters the loader for the name it is generating, which it does not today by reading, and every single-thread run would need re-measuring for no gain. The pre-existing behaviour after a failed load, where the name stays in `history` and a later load of it returns null (`InstantiatingClassloader.java:189-193`), is unchanged; by reading, not measured.
160	- **Binding a catch name always.** The grammar makes the name mandatory (`try.tex:22`), and the specification binds it (`:56-60`), so every catch clause's code changes: `getValue`, a cast and a store in place of a pop. The prelude has no `catch`, so no library class moves. The other way, binding only a name the body reads, needs a free-variable test at each clause and saves three instructions.
161	- **Binding a typecase clause's name only when it has one.** Clauses without a name pop as before, which is why only `cast`'s template changed in the prelude.

On a fixed width `n` and a count `k >= 0`, `x RSHIFT k` is `floor(x/2^k)` and `x LSHIFT k` is `x 2^k` reduced into the type modulo `2^n`. On `ZZ` the two operators are `shift(x,k)` and `shift(x,-k)`. # The C series and the APL side quest: state and what comes next

## Where the work stands

The goal is to finish what the designers intended, judged by the latest committed specification (`Specification/`, the July 2012 draft), not to redesign the language, with one program as the measuring stick: microGPT, compiled to bytecode and running fast (the root `CLAUDE.md` § Project goal; `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-16).

The live thread is the one library. The interpreter's library (`FortressLibrary` and `FortressBuiltin`) is to become the library the compiler checks, and the work is to bring the compiled checker to accept it (`coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-21). No loader in the tree registers as parallel-capable, so that lock is the loader's own monitor, the one the JVM already holds when it resolves a class through the loader. The explicit loads, `RTHelpers.loadClosureClass`, `RTHelpers.getRTTIclass` and the union instantiation, had been the only ones without it. `history` is still written before `defineClass`, safe under the lock. The gate's four-thread stage runs it as its fourteenth program, 42 PASS. Cost: none measurable. - **A typecase or catch clause's bound name is a local on the compiled path, so the compiled `cast[\T\]` matches a value of type `T`** (2026-09-28, climb batch 6.5 rung G, `<short hash>`; `compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/REPORT.md`; rows 351, 426). `CodeGen.forTypecase` binds a named clause's matched value, cast to the clause's type, as a local of a nested scope for the clause body, the shape of `forLocalVarDecl`. `CodeGen.forTry` binds the catch name to the exception's value the same way. A clause without a name is generated as before. The compiler library's `cast` template stores and reads its `y` where it had read a missing top-level object; that template is the one class of the five library jars that changes (`compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/probes/library-jars.txt`, `cast-template-javap.txt`).
